name: Kibroth-hattaavah
line: Kibroth-hattaavah was a camp in the wilderness where Israel buried people who craved other food, and its name means graves of craving.

moments.title: Graves of craving
moments.text: While the people were still eating the meat, the LORD's anger burned and He struck them with a severe plague. They named the place Kibroth-hattaavah because they buried the people who had craved other food there.

moments.title: A stop on the journey
moments.text: Israel set out from the Wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah. Then they moved on and camped at Hazeroth.

moments.title: Moving on to Hazeroth
moments.text: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.

moments.title: Making the LORD angry
moments.text: At Kibroth-hattaavah, Israel made the LORD angry. They did the same at Taberah and at Massah.
